key_insight: Local neural operators can act as data-driven surrogates for complex dynamics, making it possible to do system-level stability and bifurcation analysis without explicit equations or brute-force simulations. This combines equation-free methods with Krylov subspace techniques to extract global behavior from local learned models.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of analyzing the stability and bifurcation structure of high-dimensional spatiotemporal systems when governing equations are unavailable, too expensive to simulate, or too complex to derive analytically.
method: Train local neural operators on data to approximate the system's local evolution behavior.
Use equation-free analysis to probe macroscopic dynamics directly from the learned surrogate rather than from explicit PDEs or ODEs.
Apply Krylov subspace techniques to efficiently compute stability information and support bifurcation analysis.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how learned operators can move beyond prediction and become tools for scientific discovery and analysis. It opens a path to cheaper, equation-free study of complex systems in physics, engineering, and biology.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data -> local neural operator -> equation-free analysis -> stability/bifurcation results

Icon set showing data, neural operator, Krylov subspace, and system dynamics
paper_title: Enabling local neural operators to perform equation-free system-level analysis
paper_authors: Gianluca Fabiani, Hannes Vandecasteele, Somdatta Goswami, Constantinos Siettos, Ioannis G. Kevrekidis
